title: Hook compile map
description: The hook-capability-matrix and capability-taxonomy turned into DATA a rule compiler reads. Four tables joined on `runtime`: (1) runtime_hook_facts = the per-runtime hook surface (events, decision fields, fail modes, trust); (2) capability_expansions = how each canonical capability expands to EVERY known tool that reaches the effect, per runtime, with a normalization confidence; (3) action_bindings = which native field an authored action rides, per runtime, and whether it is functional/reserved/absent; (4) backstop_seams = which effect capabilities a non-bypassable seam guarantees. Given an authored rule (see rule.schema.json) the compiler produces, per (capability, action, runtime): {can_block, can_redact, tool_expansion, fail_mode} from the tables, then computes an honest coverage_label = MAX(hook_label, backstop_label) where hook_label = MIN across the coverage/normalization/enforcement gates. Labels are EMITTED by the compiler, never authored. Every record is sourced and dated; facts are marked vendor-doc / binary-extracted / prototype-proven vs inferred, per the project's honesty discipline. Companion spec: docs/reference/rule-compiler.md. Runtime output vocabulary it aligns to: policy-decision.schema.json.

runtime_hook_facts.description: One record per runtime: the raw hook surface. Records VENDOR facts (as documented / binary-extracted / probed), not our mitigations. The compiler's mitigations (self-deadline-to-deny, sole-rewriter) live in the label function, not here.

capability_expansions.description: One record per (runtime, capability): the fix for the per-tool-matcher leak. A canonical capability expands to every KNOWN tool that reaches the effect on that runtime, each tagged with a normalization confidence. `coverage: full` means every known tool is matched; `residual_routes` names the classify-on-sight / hook-blind remainder that is honestly NOT covered.

action_bindings.description: One record per (runtime, action): which native event+field the authored action rides, and whether that field is functional / reserved-fail-closed / absent / unverified. `emit_when` carries the reserved-field honesty rule: emit only functional fields; compile the rest to `unsupported`, never a silent downgrade.

backstop_seams.description: One record per backstop seam (matches rule.schema backstop.seam): which effect capabilities it guarantees and whether a NO there is bypassable. A non-bypassable backstop is the ONLY path to enforced-failclosed — the hook alone tops out at enforced-best-effort because no runtime fails closed on timeout.

confidence.description: Evidence tier for this record. vendor-doc = primary vendor documentation; binary-extracted = field/behavior read from the runtime binary; prototype-proven = observed in an experiments/ probe; reported = credible third party; inferred = our reasoning. Mirrors the project's [P]/[D]/[B]/[H] legend.

fieldStatus.description: functional = documented or observed working; reserved-fail-closed = present in schema but the vendor says using it DENIES the action today (Codex updatedInput/updatedPermissions/interrupt); absent = no equivalent field; unverified = present but we have not fired it (must be canary-confirmed before relied on).

normalization.description: How cleanly a call can be classified as matching the predicate. reliable = a typed tool / runtime-tagged action (YES/NO by construction); best-effort = polymorphic shell string or hostname!=resolved-IP (defeatable by obfuscation); unknown = unregistered MCP tool with no declared side-effects.

coverage.description: Of the KNOWN tools reaching this effect, how many fire a hook and are matched. full = all known tools; partial = some routes best-effort/unmatched; none = no hook fires (structural blindness); unverified = hooking is claimed but not canary-confirmed (e.g. Codex non-shell events).

coverageLabel.description: The emitted honesty label. Ordinal: unsupported(0) < advisory(1) < enforced-best-effort(2) < enforced-failclosed(3). Maps to policy-decision.enforcement: failclosed->enforced, best-effort->partially-enforced, advisory->advisory, unsupported->unsupported.

action.description: The authored rule action (rule.schema action enum).

policyDecision.description: The policy-decision.schema decision this action produces at runtime.

ref.description: URL, repo path (e.g. experiments/ccprobe/gitguard.py), or extracted binary path (e.g. /Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/codex).

events.description: The four lifecycle events the compiler targets, with the native event name and whether it fires.

decision_fields.description: The output fields that carry control, with per-runtime status. This is THE control surface (matrix section 2).

block_holds_call_open.description: True if a blocking hook (e.g. an 'ask' that awaits a human) holds the tool call suspended rather than returning fast. Enables the gitguard blocking-approval pattern; does NOT by itself defeat the runtime's own fail-open timeout.

requires_canary.description: True if coverage must be PROBED at session start (a beacon grepped from the session file), because an unregistered/untrusted/flag-off hook is silently skipped with no error.

capability.description: Canonical capability, e.g. filesystem.read (effect) or git.push_protected (domain).

capability_kind.description: effect = the taxonomy's classify-at-the-hook capability (filesystem.read, command.execute, network.egress). domain = a semantically-meaningful authored capability (git.push_protected, deploy.execute) reached THROUGH one or more effect capabilities — so it inherits their normalization/coverage.

effect_capabilities.description: For a domain capability, the effect capabilities it is reached through (e.g. git.push_protected -> [command.execute, network.egress]). Empty for effect capabilities.

matcher.description: A runtime tool name (Read), a runtime-typed action (codex:read), a shell-parse rule (bash:^\s*git\s+push), an MCP glob (mcp__*), or a raw pattern.

normalization.description: Rolled-up (weakest) normalization across the tool_matchers plus any resource-selector caveat (e.g. host:* is best-effort because hostname != resolved IP at the hook).

residual_routes.description: Known routes to the same effect that are NOT covered: hook-blind channels (auto-context, provider side-channel), unregistered MCP tools, obfuscated shell. The honest 'what leaks' list; it is what keeps `coverage: full` from over-claiming.

coverage_probed.description: True if this coverage was verified by a canary/probe (not merely asserted from config). Per the red-team: coverage must be probed, not assumed.

can_block.description: Can this action stop the effect before it happens on this runtime (deny/ask).

can_redact.description: Can this action rewrite tool output before the model sees it (redact ingress).

emit_when.description: The reserved-field honesty rule: when the compiler may emit this binding, and what to do (emit `unsupported` + surface) when the field is not functional. Never a silent downgrade to a weaker action with different semantics.

covered_effect_capabilities.description: The effect capabilities this seam guarantees a NO for (independent of the hook). '*' means the resource's own authorization governs all effects against it.

bypassable.description: false = a NO at this seam is outcome-guaranteed under the v0.1 threat model (cooperative-but-forgetful agent, not a local-root adversary). true = no guarantee (seam 'none').
